NovaBio Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone followed by the number one. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics's financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Mark Reilly, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Head of Commercial; Tom Hargrove, Head of Manufacturing; and Dr. Maria Gonzalez, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Joining me today are our CFO, Mark Reilly, and Head of R&D, Dr. Raj Patel. Before we dive into the details, I'd like to start with our overall performance highlights and key takeaways from Q3, which underscore the strength of our diversified portfolio and the momentum in our pipeline as we navigate a dynamic biotech landscape.

Overall Performance Highlights:

First and foremost, we delivered exceptional top-line results. Q3 total revenue came in at $2.85 billion, surpassing our guidance midpoint and consensus expectations by 8%, driven by a 28% year-over-year increase. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, outpacing the broader pharma index, which saw only mid-single-digit gains amid patent cliffs for legacy blockbusters like AbbVie's Humira biosimilars flooding the market.

Breaking it down by segment—our oncology franchise continues to be the growth engine, generating $1.65 billion, up 42% YoY, led by our ADC powerhouse, NovaTrastuzumab (our next-gen antibody-drug conjugate akin to Enhertu's profile), which alone contributed $1.1 billion with 55% volume growth as we expanded into HER2-low breast cancer indications post our supplemental BLA approval in Q2. Rare diseases added $650 million, +18% YoY, bolstered by steady NovaZyme uptake in Pompe disease, where we've captured 22% U.S. market share from Sanofi's gold-standard therapy.

On the profitability front, adjusted non-GAAP EPS was $1.72, beating estimates by $0.12, with gross margins expanding 320 basis points to 84.2%, thanks to manufacturing scale-up at our Singapore facility and favorable mix shift away from lower-margin gene therapies. Operating expenses rose 15% YoY to $1.1 billion, primarily R&D at $825 million (29% of revenue), reflecting accelerated investment in our bispecific T-cell engager platform and AI-driven target identification—more on that shortly. Free cash flow was robust at $950 million, up 35%, enabling $400 million in share repurchases and debt reduction.

Regionally, the U.S. remained our bedrock at 68% of revenue ($1.94B, +25% YoY), fueled by strong payer coverage for NovaTrastuzumab under Medicare Part B and a favorable CMS pricing environment post-Inflation Reduction Act negotiations. EMEA grew 36% to $520 million, with EMA approval for our CAR-T candidate LysoCyte in relapsed/refractory ALL driving uptake—European tenders awarded us preferred status in Germany and the UK, offsetting pricing pressures from HTA bodies. Asia-Pacific surged 55% to $390 million, highlighted by our partnership with Takeda in Japan, where NovaTrastuzumab launched ahead of Daiichi Sankyo's competitor, capturing 15% share in just two quarters. China remains nascent at 5% of revenue but grew triple-digits via our BeiGene collaboration, with Phase III topline data for our PD-1 inhibitor Zynara expected Q4.

From a pipeline perspective, we advanced seven programs into late-stage readouts. Notably, our CRISPR-based in vivo gene editor for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency hit 78% durable expression in the ongoing LIBERATE Phase II/III trial—on track for BLA submission H1 2025, positioning us ahead of Beam Therapeutics in this $5B addressable market. We also dosed the first patient in our AI-optimized PROTAC degrader for KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC, leveraging our proprietary AlphaFold-derived protein folding models to shave 18 months off discovery timelines.

Key Takeaways and Strategic Insights:

To crystallize the big picture: Takeaway one—our oncology and rare disease franchises are firing on all cylinders, delivering durable growth even as GLP-1 dominance from Eli Lilly's Mounjaro and Novo Nordisk's Ozempic reshapes obesity pipelines; we're staying laser-focused on high-unmet-need immuno-oncology and precision modalities like ADCs and bispecifics, where we're gaining share from Roche's Tecentriq and BMS's Opdivo.

Takeaway two—regional diversification is de-risking our profile; with U.S. policy tailwinds from the 340B carve-out expansions and Asia's patent harmonization, we now project EMEA and APAC to contribute 40% of revenue by 2027, up from 26% today.

Takeaway three—technical innovation is our moat. Our NovaAI platform, integrating single-cell RNA-seq with generative adversarial networks, has identified three novel targets since Q4 2023, with a 40% hit rate versus industry 10-15%. Partnerships like our $1.2B upfront deal with Recursion Pharmaceuticals amplify this.

Takeaway four—balance sheet fortress: $8.2B in cash, low net debt, and raised full-year 2024 guidance to $11.4-$11.8 billion revenue (24-29% growth) and $6.80-$7.20 EPS, incorporating $200M headwind from biosimilar erosion on our legacy hemophilia asset but offset by $500M from new launches.

In summary, Q3 validates our "precision growth" strategy—targeted therapies, tech-enabled R&D, and global scale. We're not just participating in biotech's resurgence; we're leading it. We are particularly excited about NOVA-101 and its potential to transform second-line metastatic breast cancer treatment with superior PFS.

Now, I will turn the call over to Mark Reilly, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mark Reilly, CFO:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.85 billion, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong volume growth in our oncology portfolio, particularly NovaTrastuzumab and Zynara, along with expanded market access in EMEA and APAC.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $1.50 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $550 million, or $1.72 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.1 billion, reflecting continued investment in R&D to support our pipeline while managing SG&A efficiencies. We continue to invest heavily in R&D, with Q3 spend at $825 million. Our cash position remains strong at $8.2 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to $11.4 to $11.8 billion in revenue and $6.80 to $7.20 non-GAAP EPS.

Before I dive deeper into our updated full-year guidance, I'd like to take a moment to outline the key assumptions underpinning our forward-looking statements, as well as the principal risk factors that could impact our trajectory. As always, these are detailed in our 10-Q filing and on Slide 25 of today's presentation. We remain committed to transparency, especially in this dynamic biotech landscape shaped by evolving regulatory environments, competitive pressures from big pharma incumbents like Roche and Pfizer, and macroeconomic headwinds.

Key Assumptions Driving Our Guidance:

Our FY2024 revenue guidance of $11.4 to $11.8 billion assumes a 24-29% year-over-year growth, primarily from our approved portfolio including Zynara (our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody for NSCLC, generating ~$850 million in trailing 12-month sales) and our CAR-T therapy, LysoCyte, which continues to ramp in the relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma market despite biosimilar erosion from the likes of Amgen's Abecma generics entering the fray. We project LysoCyte to contribute $300-350 million this year, factoring in a 5% market share expansion in the U.S. community oncology setting, driven by our expanded access program and real-world evidence data presented at ESMO last month.

Looking to 2025-2027, our long-range plan hinges on the successful commercialization of NOVA-101, our next-gen HER2-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) in Phase 3 for second-line metastatic breast cancer. We assume topline data readout in Q4 2024 with a 75% probability of meeting the primary endpoint of PFS superiority over AstraZeneca/Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu—based on our interim futility analysis and the 20% potency edge from our proprietary linker-payload technology. BLA submission to FDA by mid-2025, with PDUFA in Q1 2026, and peak U.S. sales of $2.8 billion by 2030 at a 25-30% market share, assuming list price parity (~$180K per treatment course) and 85% gross-to-net adjustments post-rebates.

Regionally, we bake in: U.S. (70% of projected revenue): CMS reimbursement at ASP +6% for NOVA-101, with no material Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) price negotiation impact until 2029, given its novel mechanism. EU (20%): Positive CHMP opinion within 12 months of EMA filing, but with 15-20% pricing concessions from HTA bodies like NICE and G-BA, reflecting recent precedents with Keytruda biosimilars. China (10%): NMPA approval via breakthrough designation in 9-12 months, leveraging our partnership with Innovent Biologics, with sales ramping to $400 million peak on 40% YoY growth amid the booming ADC market there.

Operationally, we assume R&D spend at 28% of revenue ($1.05-1.15 billion in FY2024), funding five Phase 2 assets in our oncology/rare disease pipeline, including our AI-optimized siRNA platform for NASH, which targets a 15% fibrosis regression in ongoing trials. Manufacturing scale-up at our Singapore facility—now at 120,000L capacity—supports 50% COGS improvement to 18% margins by 2026 via process intensification and continuous manufacturing. Macro assumptions include a stable 4-5% U.S. GDP growth, Fed funds rate at 3.5-4%, and biotech funding environment improving with 20-25 IPOs priced in H2 2025 per Evaluate Pharma forecasts.

Strategic enablers include our $1.2 billion cash runway through 2027 post our recent $500 million convert raise at 1.25% coupon, and bolt-on M&A like our $300 million acquisition of Synthia Therapeutics to bolster our radiopharma pipeline, mirroring Eli Lilly's Point Biopharma deal.

Principal Risk Factors:

That said, biotech is inherently high-risk, and we're not immune. Our success probabilities are calibrated conservatively using internal Bayesian models benchmarked against historical Phase 3 oncology data (e.g., ~65% approval rate per BIO stats).

Clinical and regulatory risks represent the highest probability impact: NOVA-101's Phase 3 could miss on OS (25% downside risk), triggering a 40-50% stock reaction akin to Blueprint Medicines' Ayvakit setback. Regulatory delays—e.g., FDA advisory committee scrutiny on ADC cardiac tox—could push approval to 2027, eroding $800 million in NPV. Globally, EU label restrictions or Japan's PMDA requiring bridging studies add 10-15% revenue deferral risk.

Commercial and competitive risks: Pricing pressures intensify under the IRA's $2K OOP cap and EU IVDR reforms, potentially compressing U.S. ASP by 10-12% via PBM negotiations (e.g., Express Scripts formulary exclusions). Competition from next-gen ADCs like Merck's MK-2400 or Genentech's polatuzumab successors could cap our share at 15%, halving peak sales to $1.4 billion. Biosimilar launches for Zynara by 2027 (e.g., Samsung Bioepis clones) forecast 30-40% erosion, per IQVIA models.

Operational and supply chain risks: CMC issues at our ADC fill/finish partner in Europe—amid ongoing API shortages from China tariffs—could delay launch by 6 months (15% probability). Talent retention in a tight labor market (competing with Moderna/Regeneron) risks 10% R&D productivity slip.

Macro and geopolitical risks: Recessionary pressures could slash ex-U.S. tenders by 20%, as seen with Janssen's Carvykti in Spain. China IP disputes (e.g., similar to Eli Lilly's Mounjaro litigation) pose 5-10% revenue clawback. Inflation at 3%+ erodes our 35% gross margins if raw material costs (e.g., platinum catalysts) rise 15%.

Emerging risks: Cybersecurity breaches targeting our AI drug discovery platform (partnered with Insilico Medicine) or ESG scrutiny on our palm oil-derived excipients could trigger 5-10% EPS dilution from fines/litigation.

In aggregate, our base case achieves 25% CAGR to $3.5 billion revenue by 2028 with 22% operating margins, but a severe downside scenario (e.g., NOVA-101 failure + IRA acceleration) limits us to $1.8 billion and cash burn through 2026. We'll mitigate via disciplined capital allocation—prioritizing KOL engagement, patient registries for label expansions, and scenario planning in our ERP system.

We believe these assumptions are achievable given our derisked profile, but outcomes depend on execution.

Now, turning to R&D expenses and pipeline investment priorities, which remain the lifeblood of NovaBio Therapeutics as we advance our industry-leading portfolio in oncology, rare diseases, and immunology. In Q3, R&D expenses totaled $825 million, up 25% year-over-year from the prior-year period. This increase reflects our aggressive investment in late-stage assets and platform technologies, partially offset by milestone efficiencies from prior partnerships. For the full year 2024, we continue to guide R&D spend at $1.05 billion to $1.15 billion, representing about 28% of our projected revenue—consistent with our peers like Regeneron and Vertex, but with a sharper focus on high-ROI modalities.

Breaking it down by key categories: Oncology commanded 42% of our Q3 spend, or roughly $347 million, driven by our next-gen ADCs. Our lead ADC, NOVA-101, targeting HER2-low breast cancer—a market opportunity we estimate at $15 billion globally by 2030—progressed seamlessly into Phase III enrollment, with topline data expected in H2 2025. We're allocating an additional $50 million this year to combo studies with PD-1 inhibitors.

Rare diseases took 28%, or $231 million, with heavy emphasis on gene therapies. Our AAV-based candidate for Duchenne muscular dystrophy hit a key inflection point with positive Phase IIb data showing 35% dystrophin expression uplift versus benchmarks. This program's burn supports a BLA filing in mid-2025, tapping into a $5 billion addressable market.

Immunology accounted for 20%, or $165 million, prioritizing bispecific T-cell engagers for autoimmune conditions. Early Phase II data showed 85% response rates, fueling a ramp-up for pivotal trials.

The remaining 10% went to platform investments—our NovaAI engine has cut hit-to-lead timelines by 40% in PROTACs for oncology targets. We're also scaling LNP tech for future applications.

Our spend profile reflects industry shifts: 15-20% YoY R&D inflation, but we're outperforming on efficiency. Geographically, 55% U.S.-centric, 25% Europe, 15% APAC via partnerships, 5% manufacturing scale-up.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 R&D at similar levels, with key milestones ahead.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Chen, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Mark. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, NOVA-101 remains on track with interim data supporting PFS superiority, and our CRISPR gene editor showed 78% durable expression in LIBERATE. LysoCyte expansion in ALL is gaining traction post-EMA approval. We expect to report topline Phase 3 data for Zynara in China Q4 and file BLA for our DMD gene therapy H1 2025. Upcoming milestones include two Phase 3 readouts H1 2025 and first patient dosed in KRAS PROTAC trial.

Next, Dr. Raj Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Our NovaAI platform has identified three novel targets with a 40% hit rate, accelerating discovery for siRNA in NASH and PROTACs in NSCLC. We're advancing AI-optimized bispecifics and CRISPR editing for rare diseases, with INDs planned H2 2025. Partnerships with Recursion are amplifying output.

Now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Raj. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with total net product revenues of $2.85 billion, up 28% year-over-year. We are seeing strong uptake in NovaTrastuzumab and Zynara across key market segments. Our marketing campaigns are proving effective in driving NBRx growth and formulary wins.

Let me turn to our new product launches and the impressive market share momentum across our portfolio. Fiscal 2024 has been transformative, with launches driving outsized growth in oncology. Starting with NovaTrastuzumab, launched Q4 2023—Q3 net sales hit $1.1 billion, 55% volume growth, capturing 12% U.S. market share per IQVIA. NBRx surged, refill rates at 78%, with 85% formulary coverage. We're gearing for EU launch Q4.

For LysoCyte, our bispecific for R/R LBCL, Q3 sales $300 million, 18% market share, with HCP adoption up 150% QoQ. Hospital penetration 92%.

Market share expanded 450 bps YoY. Our launch playbook—DTC, KOLs, patient hubs—is key. Raising FY guidance for these to $2.4-2.6 billion.

On geographic revenue breakdown, U.S. 68% at $1.94 billion, up 25%. EMEA 18% $520 million, up 36%. APAC 11% $390 million +55%, China triple-digits.

Emerging markets ex-China grew 32% to 12.6% of total, India +41% via biosimilars, Brazil +28%, SE Asia +35%, Africa +50%. China +27%. Pillars: localized JVs, adaptive pricing, supply resilience. Expect 15-18% by 2025.

Our marketing is driving share gains amid competition.

Next, Tom Hargrove will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Tom Hargrove, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Sarah. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Capacity at Singapore now 120,000L, 95% utilization for ADCs, driving COGS to 18% target by 2026 via continuous processes. Devens site scaling Q1 2025, cutting COGS 15%. Supply chain resilient with regional hubs, mitigating API shortages and tariffs. Focused on CMC for NOVA-101 launch and CAR-T fill/finish.

Finally, Dr. Maria Gonzalez will provide an update on regulatory submissions and approvals.

Dr. Maria Gonzalez, Head of Regulatory Affairs:
Thank you, Tom. We continue to work closely with regulatory agencies. Recent wins include EMA for LysoCyte, supplemental BLA for NovaTrastuzumab. NOVA-101 BLA mid-2025, PDUFA Q1 2026. Ongoing interactions: FDA on ADC tox, EMA CHMP positive, PMDA bridging, NMPA breakthrough for China. On pricing and reimbursement, U.S. GTN 42%, WAC stable, IRA modeled $200-300M headwind by 2027, countered by RWE. EU HTA 7.2 months avg, net ASP down 4%, Japan NHI premium. Emerging tiered pricing. AI analytics optimize rebates.

On patent cliff exposure for Zynara, expiring Q3 2026 U.S., modeled 75-85% erosion $2.1-2.4B headwind. Mitigated by XR formulation to 2032, label expansions SVR12 82%, pediatric extensions, next-gen combos. M&A diversifies. Net impact 15% vs. sector 25%.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Elena.

Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you, Maria. In closing, our Q3 results and pipeline momentum position NovaBio for sustained growth. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Jane Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jane Doe, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, good morning. Elena, can you elaborate on revenue guidance and key catalysts ahead, especially around NOVA-101?

Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thanks, Jane. Mark, do you want to take that?

Mark Reilly, CFO:
Sure, Elena. For full year 2024, raising revenue to $11.4-11.8 billion, 24-29% growth. Oncology 65%, immunology 22%, rare 10%. U.S. 72%, Europe 18%, ex-U.S. growth 8%. Catalysts: Q4 PDUFA NOVA-101 expansion ORR 42% PFS 14 mo, $1.2B peak. H1 2025 Phase 3 for bispecific UC and DMD expansion. Partnerships $1.5B Lilly-like, Japan out-license. Capacity Q1, China BLA. Positions for 20%+ CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Chen, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. Sarah, thoughts on emerging market growth and how it fits long-term?

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Commercial:
Thanks, Mike. Emerging ex-China 32% to 12.6%, ahead of 25-30% CAGR guide. India biosimilars 18% share, Brazil tenders, SE Asia HPV, Africa malaria. China 27% ramp NRDL. Access 2030: JVs CAR-T LatAm, tiered pricing 40-60% off, $250M hubs. To 15-18% by 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Grant with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Grant, Morgan Stanley:
Hi team. On patent cliff and LCM strategies?

Dr. Maria Gonzalez, Head of Regulatory Affairs:
Hi Lisa. Zynara cliff Q3 2026, 75-85% drop modeled. XR patent 2032 25% share capture, combo SVR12 sNDA Q4 $1.2B, pediatric 6 mo extension. NeoVira-STAT3 Ph Ib, M&A AuraBio ADC $900M NPV. 18% R&D to LCM, net 15% impact.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee, Barclays:
Thanks. Pricing dynamics in U.S./EU?

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Commercial:
Tom, U.S. GTN 42%, rebates 28%, copay 8%, 340B 6%. IRA headwind modeled, RWE 22% A1c superior, 85% preferred formulary. EU 18% discounts, AMNOG MEA, NICE 22% off. Japan 12% premium, China 32% NRDL. AI sims, bundles reduce spend 14%.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Elena Vasquez, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
